why: Dogfood cycle 3 (docs/v3/cycles/dogfood-3.md) logged one P1. dogfood-3.2: no selected or open table row is visibly marked. `body.tsx:186` sets `data-selected` and `aria-current` on the row whose detail is open (and `data-selected` on a ticked row), and `table/table.css:57-62` paints it with `var(--basalt-surface-row-selected)`, a 2.x name the v3 sheet never emits: `packages/basalt-ui/dist/styles.css` has no `row-selected` at all, and v3's token map (`tokens/table.ts:137`) names the role `selected` with `tw: ['--color-selected']`. In Chrome on the built playground the open row #642 reads `aria-current=true`, `data-selected=""`, `--basalt-surface-row-selected` empty and a transparent background, in light and dark, on a deep link and after a click (`.evidence/cycle-dogfood-3/probe3.log`; crops `.evidence/cycle-dogfood-3/crops/marked-row-{light,dark}.png`). The console tints the peeked row `bg-accent` (`components/flow/issue-table.tsx:58`). Cycles 1 and 2 checked the attribute, never the pixels. `tokens/row-surfaces.test.ts` still asserts `--basalt-surface-row-selected:` in the 2.x-era emitter, and `basalt-resolves.test.ts` holds only the `BASALT` refs to the v3 sheet, not the CSS files.
what: A selected or open table row is tinted again, in both schemes.
owns: packages/basalt-ui/src/table/table.css (the selected and focused row rules)
the v3 token the rule reads, if it is not emitted (packages/basalt-ui/src/tokens/*, the generated sheet)
a layout test beside the table's layout tests
change: Point the selected row rules in `table/table.css` at the variable the v3 sheet emits for the `selected` role (today `--color-selected`), and make sure the sheet emits it even when no utility class uses it. Then sweep `src/**/*.css` for any other `var(--...)` the v3 sheet does not define and fix those the same way, or name them in the PR. Add a guard so a CSS file can no longer read an undefined token: a unit test that every `var(--...)` in the shipped CSS resolves to a declared variable, or the existing token check extended to CSS files.
proof: make check-fast; a layout test that reads the computed background of an `aria-current` row and of a ticked row and finds it opaque and different from an unmarked row in light and dark; the guard test failing on the old `table.css`.
acceptance: An open row and a ticked row have a non-transparent background different from their neighbours in light and dark (layout test)
